head: Head of this branch: `bcbaae6`, on top of `237bb07a`. Two commits, three source files and three test files, 0 lines removed from any public contract.
came_from:
The house deep gate ran two lenses over the landed R-B4 fix against three pre-registered falsification targets, with the kill rule fixed before the run: a target dies only to an executed call sequence naming file, function and line, never to an argument. The second-family lens agreed on all three targets while two of its three reasons were wrong, so its agreement was not counted as corroboration and an independent run followed. That run refuted the third target, and the sentence it refuted is in this repository, written by the same session that wrote the fix.

| Target | Verdict | How it was settled |
|---|---|---|
| F1, a path where `passed` reaches a signed artefact with no bool establisher on it | held | seven signing calls executed with `passed` in {`"false"`, `0`, `"0"`, `[]`, `{}`}, every one refused, no artefact produced |
| F2, an establisher whose return value is discarded while a later site re-reads the field raw | held | the one discarding site is followed by a second full establishment, executed |
| F3, the refusals are typed so differently that one `except` cannot catch them | refuted | two executed proofs, in the next block |
defect:
The docstring of the sixth R-B4 site promised that one `except` covers this function. Its second half was true and is kept: all five R-B4 sites raise `BundleFormatError`, so one `except BundleFormatError` covers those five. What it left out is what a reader takes from the sentence before it, and that omission is the defect.

So `issue_sd_jwt` has two disjoint refusal families, and a third form exists one layer out that is not an exception at all. No single `except` covers the module's refusals. This is a documentation defect and not a hole: every refusal fires, only their form differs, and a caller who believed the sentence would route the R-B4 refusal into the wrong error path.

The same lens run reported a second finding. `intoto._require_bool_verdict` and `sdjwt_issue._require_bool_verdict` were two independent implementations with no shared import and the same intent, so a future change at one site would forget the other. That is the class this package has paid for four times: the hashable-membership class became a module only after three instance fixes, the `(x or {})` class became `as_dict` for the same reason, R-B4 itself had a sixth site because five of six lived in one file, and then R-B4's own fix produced two copies of its own guard.
fix:
The sentence is replaced by what is measured, and the measurement moved into a contract, because prose about exception types goes stale without anything breaking, which is exactly what happened to the sentence being replaced.

`src/proofbundle/_verdict.py` now holds the single `require_bool_verdict(claim, wo=...)`, and both `intoto.py` and `sdjwt_issue.py` import it. It is deliberately not in `_membership.py`, where `is_bool` lives: that module has no package imports at all and is imported by nine others precisely for that reason, while this function needs `errors.BundleFormatError`.

The first contract carries three guards rather than catch proofs alone, because a file that only proved that two excepts do not overlap would also pass if the refusals stopped happening: a valid claim still decodes with a bool verdict, a valid claim is still issued as a compact SD-JWT, and the half of the docstring that was right is pinned as its own case.

measured.what: except ValueError around issue_sd_jwt with passed="false"
except ProofBundleError around issue_sd_jwt with a malformed status
decode_eval_claim on a signed bundle whose passed is "false"
implementations of the verdict establisher in the package
cases in the two new contracts
cases of the one-establisher contract falling against the pre-merge tree
measured.source: git stash of the three source files, then pytest

measured.what: neighbouring R-B4 contracts after the merge

not_changed:
No public signature, no error type, and no refusal behaviour. Every value that was refused before is refused now, with the same exception class at the same site; only the message text changed, and no test asserted on it.

The shared message no longer says that the refusal protects the always-open claims of a validly signed SD-JWT. That is a real loss and not a cleanup: it was the sharpest half of that refusal. One message cannot carry four sites' consequences, so the site name is passed in and the consequence moved into a comment at the call site.

The truthiness scanner keeps the old private name in its establisher set on purpose. A name that once established the type must not start counting as a plain read if it ever comes back, and dropping it would silently widen what that scanner lets through.

The full suite over the committed tree was started after the commit rather than before it, so the measured surface stands still for its duration; its verdict was still running when this source was written and is therefore not stated here. Two families ran over this change, the floor for a deep verdict is three, and no deep-gate verdict is claimed for it.
